question.problem:
A mountain valley is monitoring the population of a reintroduced elk herd. The valley can sustain a maximum population of $600$ elk, but the herd is still below this limit. Since ecologists began tracking the growth, the population reached $536$ elk on month $4$ and $573$ elk on month $10.$ On what month will the population reach $590$ elk? Round your answer to the nearest integer.

*Hint: You may assume that the population of elk, $P(t),$ increases at a rate that obeys an inhibited growth model, where $t$ is the time, in months.*
question.worked_solution:
The rate at which the population $P(t)$ changes is proportional to the difference between the maximum population and its current population. Therefore, we have the inhibited growth equation

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=k(a-P),
$$

where $a$ is the maximum population the valley can sustain, and $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality.

In our case, $a=600$ elk, and we have

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=k(600-P).
$$

First, we integrate our differential equation by separating the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dP}{600-P} & =k\,dt \\ \int \frac{dP}{600-P} & =\int k\,\text{d}t \\ -\operatorname{ln}⁡|600-P| & =kt+C\end{aligned}
$$

Since this is the solution to an inhibited growth equation, we have $600-P>0$ for all $t\ge 0.$ Next, we solve for $P(t),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}600-P & ={e}^{-kt-C} \\ 600-P & ={e}^{-C}{e}^{-kt} \\ 600-P & =K{e}^{-kt} \\ P & =600-K{e}^{-kt}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $K={e}^{-C}$ is a constant of integration.

We're told that, on month $4,$ the population was $536$ elk. So, applying the condition $P(4)=536,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(4) & =536 \\ 600-K{e}^{-4k} & =536 \\ K{e}^{-4k} & =64.\end{aligned}
$$

We're also told that, on month $10,$ the population was $573$ elk. So, applying the condition $P(10)=573,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(10) & =573 \\ 600-K{e}^{-10k} & =573 \\ K{e}^{-10k} & =27.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, by dividing the result of the first condition by the result of the second, we can solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{K{e}^{-4k}}{K{e}^{-10k}} & =\frac{64}{27} \\ {e}^{6k} & =\frac{64}{27} \\ 6k & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{64}{27}) \\ k & =\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{64}{27})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting back into the result of the first condition, we solve for $K:$

$$
\begin{aligned}K{e}^{-4\cdot (1/6)\operatorname{ln}⁡(64/27)} & =64 \\ K & =64{e}^{(4/6)\operatorname{ln}⁡(64/27)} \\ K & =64{e}^{(2/3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(64/27)} \\ K & =64{(\frac{64}{27})}^{2/3} \\ K & =\frac{1\,024}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following expression for $P(t):$

$$
P(t)=600-\frac{1\,024}{9}{e}^{-(t/6)\operatorname{ln}⁡(64/27)}.
$$

Finally, let $m$ be the month when the population reaches $590$ elk. Then, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(m) & =590 \\ 600-\frac{1\,024}{9}{e}^{-km} & =590 \\ 10 & =\frac{1\,024}{9}{e}^{-km} \\ {e}^{-km} & =\frac{90}{1\,024} \\ {e}^{-km} & =\frac{45}{512} \\ -km & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{45}{512}) \\ m & =-\frac{1}{k}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{45}{512}).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting in our value for $k,$ we conclude that the population will be $590$ elk on month

$$
m=\frac{-\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{45}{512})}{\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{64}{27})}=16.905…≈17,
$$

rounded to the nearest day.
